feature: A stack can be a fixed size and its rows fill it
summary: A group that stacks itself can now be given a width and a height instead of only being as big as what is in it, so a menu can be 320 wide and every row can fill it without building it on a screen. Padding works on one of these groups too, not just on a screen.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Flags on by default (Groups that arrange their own contents).

try.do: Draw three rectangles of different widths, one under the other.
Select all three and press Control-Command-G (Layer > Stack Selection).
Type 320 into W in Position & Size and press Return.
In the Layout section, set Horizontal to Stretch.
Type 16 into Padding in the Layout section.
Type 300 into H, then press Command-Z.
In the Layout section, press Hug on the Width row.
Drag the stack's right handle wider and watch what happens to the rows.

evaluate: When you typed 320 into W, did you expect the rows to widen by themselves, or was the Horizontal Stretch step where you would have looked?
Is the Layout section's caption doing that job, or did you read past it?
Do Width and Height belong under Direction, or would you look for them beside the W and H boxes above?
Is Hug the right word for a group that is as big as what is inside it?
Dragging a handle now sizes the stack rather than magnifying its contents. Is that what your hand expected?
rough: Screenshots here are real window captures from the loop's own probe app, not offscreen renders.

A stack told it is 320 wide does not widen its rows on its own: the Horizontal row still owns that axis. Mocks usually draw a per-child hug/fill/fixed control instead. That control is still cut, because it would say the same thing twice, but it means the feature takes two steps rather than one.
There is no distribution yet, so a stack taller than its rows leaves the spare room at the bottom rather than spreading them out.
No minimum or maximum size, and padding is still one number for all four sides.
A stack set to Stretch inside another container quietly gets a fixed size of its own from that container. If you later stop stretching it, it keeps the size it was last given until you press Hug.
